slug: 2026-05-15 African Commission Highlighting pressures on civic space in Kenya and Rwanda
note: ARTICLE 19 Eastern Africa is not a body inside Rwanda and names no policy; the arrests of content creators and opposition figures are general, with no person, date, words or law stated; no cut, repeal or no-punishment statement.
Government guidelines on citizens' assemblies; no criticism, cut or penalty stated (a consultation-type channel, other).
Resolutions of a government dialogue forum; states no criticism by a named outside body, no cut and no penalty.
Strategy passage on media capacity and planned media-law amendments; states no dated criticism, cut or penalty.
Ingabire arrest is for alleged criminal group and public disorder, not stated as speech and over twelve months before 2026-08-31; the Article 39 ruling upholds a speech law and is no repeal or use.
Named only for a national AI strategy.
Government statement on law revisions; no criticism, cut or punishment of speech stated.

facts.fact: RSF states that journalist Dieudonne Niyonsenga (Ishema TV) was sentenced to seven years in prison for 'humiliating' state officials in 2021, and was still jailed in July 2024.
RSF states that Theoneste Nsengimana, director of Umubavu TV, was arrested in October 2021 while organising an event with opposition leader Victoire Ingabire, and was still held in July 2024.

note: Freedom House report; only a biometric SIM-registration rule, not a national ID system fact or anything these studies ask.

facts.fact: An ARM project policy brief says that in 2019 the Rwandan Senate accused 26 online radio stations and websites of exiled critics of genocide denial and the websites were made inaccessible, with the regulator RURA giving no explanation or appeal.

note: Nothing on public debate, cuts or punishment.
The document states nothing this study asks of this country.

facts.fact: ARTICLE 19 told the UPR pre-session on 27 November 2025 that independent online news sites including The Rwandan and Le Prophete, and local diaspora platforms, remain blocked; it does not say who ordered the block.
ARTICLE 19 says journalists and online commentators continue to face arrests and prosecutions for speech offences, and several independent YouTube-based journalists have been detained or intimidated.
